name: Checked CFP exam results and passed.
description: At exactly 7 o'clock, I took a deep breath and logged into the CFP exam system. When I saw the eye-catching word “Pass,” the anxiety, exhaustion, and pressure of the past months melted away in an instant. I was stunned, not overjoyed, but feeling a kind of weakness and numbness after an immense relief. My husband Zhang Weiming walked in quietly from behind me, placed a glass of warm water in my hand, and without speaking, just patted my shoulder. My throat tightened, and I whispered, “I passed.” He turned and walked to the kitchen to fry me an egg.
location: Bedroom at home, Block 2, Whampoa Garden Residential Estate, Hung Hom, Kowloon City District, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region

name: Breakfast and decision to take leave
description: I sat down at the dining table in front of a bowl of plain congee, a fried egg, and a small plate of fermented tofu. I quietly told my mother and husband the result, and they were both happy for me. I felt completely drained, and exhaustion swept over me. I decided to rest thoroughly for the whole day. My mother, Chen Meiling, said readily, "Sleep easy, I've got things at home."
location: Dining room at home, Block 2, Whampoa Garden Residential Estate, Hung Hom, Kowloon City District, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region

name: Catch up on deep sleep
description: The tension in my nerves suddenly released, and a wave of exhaustion hit me. I drew the curtains tight, changed into cotton pajamas, and fell asleep almost instantly once I lay back down. Those two and a half hours were complete rest—I didn't even dream. I needed the sleep to repay the debt I had incurred from staying up late for days.
location: Master bedroom at home, Block 2, Whampoa Garden Residential Estate, Hung Hom, Kowloon City District, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region

name: Wake-up and message handling
description: After waking up naturally, my body still felt a bit heavy, but my mood had improved. I picked up my phone and first replied to several routine greeting messages from regular clients — Mrs. Chan asked if I needed her to bring groceries this morning, and I told her I was on leave today. Then I opened MyFitnessPal, logged the caffeine intake from last night to this morning (one cup of strong tea), thought about it, and deleted it. I had a glass of warm water and drank it slowly.
location: Living room at home, Block 2, Whampoa Garden Residential Estate, Hung Hom, Kowloon City District, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region

name: Rest again and light recovery
description: I decided not to push myself. After drinking some water, I went back to the bedroom, leaned against the headboard, opened Liang Shiqiu's Yashe Sketches and read for half an hour, then listened to the sound of rain pattering against the window. Later, drowsiness came over me again, so I simply took a nap for about an hour. When I woke up, I felt much more refreshed. I went to the living room, where my mother was picking over vegetables. She said, 'Come over and sit once you're awake.'
location: At home in Block 2, Whampoa Garden Residential Estate, Hung Hom, Kowloon City District, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region

name: Light lunch
description: Mother had already cooked a pot of plain rice porridge, plus stir-fried baby bok choy and steamed grass carp belly. I carefully logged in MyFitnessPal: “1 bowl of plain rice porridge, 150g stir-fried baby bok choy, 100g steamed grass carp belly.” Light and nutritious, just to my liking. After the meal, I felt much lighter in both stomach and body.
location: Dining room at home, Block 2, Whampoa Garden Residential Estate, Hung Hom, Kowloon City District, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region

name: Afternoon relaxation and checking on a friend
description: I leaned on the sofa and continued listening to music, then picked up my phone and sent a WeChat message to my close friend Lin Jiaxin: "Jiaxin, I passed the exam, and today I'm so exhausted that I'm lying flat at home. What about you? If something is on your mind, come talk to me." There was no reply after the message was sent. I was a bit worried, so I contacted my best friend in Shenzhen, Huang Wenhui: "Ah Hui, have you been in touch with Jiaxin lately? She was laid off last Friday. Yesterday I went to Sham Shui Po to find her, but she didn't see me. I'm a little worried about her. Could you check on her for me?" After sending the message, I stared blankly at the raindrops falling again outside the window.
location: Living room at home, Block 2, Whampoa Garden Residential Estate, Hung Hom, Kowloon City District, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region

name: Sofa in the living room and study, Whampoa Garden residence, Kowloon City District, Hong Kong
description: After recovering mentally, I decided to do some light work. I went into the study, carefully sorted and bound the CFP review materials stacked on the desk (the mistake collection, formula sheets, and notebooks), and put them in a file folder for temporary storage. Then I opened my laptop, created a new folder named "Career Growth [Second Half of 2025]," and listed a few key points: how to apply what I've learned to developing comprehensive plans for high-net-worth clients, planning to attend the company's August advanced wealth management training, and considering obtaining the CPB (private banker) certificate. My thinking gradually became clearer.
location: Home study, Block 2, Whampoa Garden residential estate, Hung Hom, Kowloon City District, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region

name: Short break and supermarket shopping
description: I stood up and stretched. My mother reminded me that the light soy sauce and steamed fish soy sauce at home were almost used up and that she needed to cook dinner in the evening. I responded, saying I would go downstairs to buy them in a bit. Then I changed into casual home clothes, took a reusable bag, and walked about 5 minutes to the Wellcome supermarket downstairs. Following the list, I bought Lee Kum Kee light soy sauce and steamed fish soy sauce, and also picked up a pack of children's growing-up cheese for the kids. When passing the snack aisle, I grabbed a bottle of unsweetened oolong tea for myself. After checking out, I walked home.
location: Wellcome supermarket, G/F, Whampoa New Town Shopping Mall, 6 Tak Hong Street, Kowloon City District, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.

name: Return home and take a short rest
description: When I got home, I handed the shopping bags to my mother, then sat on the sofa and took a few sips of unsweetened oolong tea. When I checked my phone, I received a reply from Huang Wenhui: "Jiaxin got back to me. She said she'll be fine in a while, no need to worry. You should also get some rest." I felt a little relieved.
location: Living room at home, Block 2, Whampoa Garden Residential Estate, Hung Hom, Kowloon City District, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region

name: Preparing the meal with mother
description: I tied on an apron and walked into the kitchen. I took the grass carp out of the fridge, carefully scraped off the scales, removed the innards, made a few cuts on both sides of the fish, and marinated it with a thin layer of salt and shredded ginger. My mother was washing choy sum beside me, picking off the old leaves. We chatted while working: Mother mentioned that when she met our neighbor Mrs. Li downstairs that afternoon, they talked about how Mrs. Li's daughter had also recently passed the civil service exam. I smiled and said, "That's a good thing." While prepping the ingredients, I poured some steamed fish soy sauce into a small dish for later, and a steady sense of calm rose in my heart.
location: Home kitchen, Block 2, Whampoa Garden residential estate, Hung Hom, Kowloon City District, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region

name: Preparing dinner while the family waits
description: I filled the steamer with water, ready to turn on the heat once my husband and children arrived home. My mother was stir-frying choy sum in the kitchen, and I cleaned up the stove area. Then the doorbell rang—I knew it was my husband back from picking up my son from school.
location: Home kitchen, Block 2, Whampoa Garden residential estate, Hung Hom, Kowloon City District, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region

name: Enjoyed dinner with family
description: Husband Zhang Weiming picked up their son Zhang Zixuan from school and came home. The whole family sat around the table together. Dinner included my mother's signature steamed grass carp, stir-fried choy sum with garlic, and half a roast goose that Zhang Weiming had specially bought from the roast meat shop downstairs. The children chattered about funny things from school. I filled a bowl of white rice for myself and carefully recorded: 1 bowl of white rice, steamed fish, garlic choy sum, 2 pieces of roast goose. Looking at this lively, heartwarming scene, I was filled with contentment.
location: Dining room at home, Block 2, Whampoa Garden Residential Estate, Hung Hom, Kowloon City District, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region

name: Parent-child time and homework tutoring
description: After the meal, I accompanied my son Zhang Zixuan back to his room to check his math homework. He had gotten two word problems wrong, and I patiently guided him to re-analyze the problem statements and correct the mistakes. Then he proudly showed me a paper airplane he had made in school arts and crafts class, and I praised him for doing a good job. After that, I went to the living room and played with my daughter Zhang Yuxin with puzzles for fifteen minutes, then read her Chapter 20 of The Little Prince. My husband Zhang Weiming was responsible for clearing the table and washing the dishes.
location: At home in Block 2, Whampoa Garden Residential Estate, Hung Hom, Kowloon City District, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region

name: Online communication and relaxation with running buddies
description: After the children played on their own, I leaned back on the living room sofa to rest and called my running buddy Shen Peiwen. We talked for half an hour: I told her I passed the exam today, she congratulated me and said, "Resume training tomorrow!" We discussed the long-run plan for this Saturday morning (June 7) — because the forecast called for showers, Shen Peiwen suggested that if it rained, we would go to Kowloon Walled City Park to run loops instead, since there is a sheltered corridor there. We agreed to meet at the park's main gate at 7 a.m. on Saturday. After hanging up, I felt a bit more relaxed.
location: Living room at home, Block 2, Whampoa Garden Residential Estate, Hung Hom, Kowloon City District, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region

name: Cantonese embroidery and personal time
description: I took out the Cantonese embroidery frame I hadn't touched for a long time and embroidered a butterfly wing under the soft light on the balcony. The silk thread moved through my fingers; my movements were very slow, and I focused on the stitches as they went along — at this moment, work pressure and exam anxiety both felt far away from me. I listened to the faint sounds of my family moving around in the living room, and felt a long-missed sense of peace and calm in my heart.
location: Balcony at home, Block 2, Whampoa Garden residential estate, Hung Hom, Kowloon City District, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region

name: Bedtime preparation and sleep
description: After embroidering for about 45 minutes, I began to feel drowsy. I put away my embroidery frame and took a hot shower, washing away the day's fatigue. After washing up, I ironed the shirt I would wear tomorrow and hung it on the wardrobe door handle, marked several client to-dos on my phone calendar that needed priority handling in the morning, and set the 6:45 wake-up alarm. I changed into my pajamas and lay down, looking back on the day—from the tension in the early morning, the exhaustion after checking the results, to the relaxation in the afternoon and the warm family gathering in the evening, it felt like a very long dream. I said softly to my husband beside me, "Thank you, Wei Ming. It feels so good to have gotten through this." He squeezed my hand and said, "You've worked hard. Get some sleep soon." With the joy of passing the exam and the relief of a burden lifted, I soon fell into a deep sleep.
location: At home in Block 2, Whampoa Garden Residential Estate, Hung Hom, Kowloon City District, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region

name: Morning wake-up and yoga
description: After the alarm rang, she did simple stretching in bed for 5 minutes to shake off drowsiness. Then she laid out a yoga mat in front of the living room's floor-to-ceiling window and did a 20-minute Yin Yoga practice, focusing on Butterfly Pose, seated forward fold, and spinal twist to release tension in the back and hips. After finishing, she went to the kitchen to help her mother prepare breakfast ingredients and confirmed that the children's school items for today were all ready.
location: Whampoa Garden Residential Estate, 328 Prince Edward Road West, Kowloon City District, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region

name: Family morning and commute preparation
description: Helped her mother prepare breakfast and lunch boxes for the children. Woke up her son and daughter and urged them to wash up and get dressed. Had a brief talk with her husband Weiming about today's drop-off and pick-up arrangements (he would take their son to Kowloon Tong Government Primary School, and her mother would take their daughter to Kowloon City Kindergarten). Packed her own commuter bag and checked for any missing documents.
location: Whampoa Garden Residential Estate, 328 Prince Edward Road West, Kowloon City District, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region

name: Metro commuting and browsing news.
description: Walk to Mong Kok East Station, take the East Rail Line to Admiralty Station, transfer to the Island Line, and arrive at Wan Chai Station. The whole journey is about 42 minutes. On the train, she used her phone to listen to a financial news podcast and quickly browsed clients' Moments posts, liking posts from several potential clients.
location: Along the MTR line from Mong Kok East Station to Wan Chai Station in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.

name: Breakfast and diet record
description: At Mak's Noodle near the company, she ordered a bowl of shrimp wonton noodles. While waiting, she opened the food diary app, logged the breakfast (a bowl of wonton noodles, leaving some of the soup), and backfilled the dinner information she had forgotten to log yesterday.
location: Mak's Noodle (First Commercial Building), 37 Leighton Road, Wan Chai District, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region

name: Morning work: emails and client follow-up.
description: It took about 18 minutes on foot from Mak's Noodle to the office. She first logged into the system and processed 20 backlogged emails, of which 3 were client inquiries that needed replies. Then, following the planned checklist, she successfully contacted the two potential clients on the list by phone and scheduled face-to-face meetings at the office for next Tuesday and Thursday at 10 a.m. Meanwhile, she sent a WeChat message to Chen Meiling (Mrs. Chen), trying to arrange for her to come in next Wednesday afternoon for the annual policy review.
location: AIA office, Immigration Tower, 7 Gloucester Road, Wan Chai District, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region

name: Received visiting clients and organized documents
description: Received a client who made an appointment through a referral for an in-home consultation about critical illness insurance. Based on her situation of being 35 years old and having a family, she explained in detail the brochures and premium differences of two savings-type critical illness plans, and left the product materials and her business card. After seeing the client off, she organized the consultation notes and began preparing a PPT outline on "Policy Anniversary Review Process" for next week's team training.
location: AIA office, Immigration Tower, 7 Gloucester Road, Wan Chai District, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region

name: Midday networking lunch.
description: Colleague Su Lishan and I walked about 9 minutes from the office to Capital Café for lunch. Ordered a set meal (satay beef instant noodles with scrambled egg and toast), and also added the cucumber salad and braised beef from my own lunchbox as extra dishes. The two of us mainly talked about He Junwen's problem. Su Lishan explained in detail how messy his document filing was, and we decided to take time next Monday afternoon to personally walk him through the whole process. When asked about Lin Jiaxin, Su Lishan said she had also been rarely replying to group messages lately, and there was no progress with Huang Wenhui either, so we decided to ask Huang Wenhui out to meet and talk over the weekend.
location: Capital Cafe (Heard Street), 6 Heard Street, Wan Chai District, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region

name: Midday rest and snack record
description: After lunch, instead of going straight back to the office, she walked about 5 minutes from Huaxing Café to a bench at Harbour Road Garden and sat for 20 minutes, soaking up the sun and digesting. She used the app to retroactively log an apple she had as a mid-morning snack, then returned to the office.
location: Harbour Road Garden, 28 Harbour Road, Wan Chai District, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region

name: Afternoon work: client materials and training preparation
description: Back at my desk, I focused on completing the afternoon's work. First, I entered the needs analysis from the morning client meeting into the system and created a follow-up task. Then I continued the team training PPT I had left unfinished in the morning, designing an interactive segment where newcomers could role-play scripts for responding after a client says no. In the middle of this, I received a call from actuarial colleague Guo Junwei, and we had a brief technical discussion about a new product.
location: AIA office, Immigration Tower, 7 Gloucester Road, Wan Chai District, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region

name: Team communication and internal coordination
description: Confirmed a commission calculation detail for the new product with Guo Junwei on WeChat. Then I went to Miss Zhao, the department assistant, to verify whether the reservation time for next week's team training room was accurate. Back at my seat, I handled some miscellaneous paperwork and filed the day's completed documents.
location: AIA office, Immigration Tower, 7 Gloucester Road, Wan Chai District, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region

name: Yin yoga class
description: After work, walked to the yoga studio and caught the 17:45 yin yoga class. Guided by the teacher, through long-held poses (such as Saddle Pose, Shoelace Pose, and Snail Pose), I deeply stretched my hips, thighs, and spine. After the class, I felt the tension in my body and the pressure in my mind were released. After class, I exchanged a few words with a yoga classmate I know well about weekend class arrangements.
location: Pure Yoga studio, Hopewell Centre, Wan Chai District, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region

name: Commuting and shopping along the way
description: Walk from Hopewell Centre to Wan Chai Station, take the MTR back to Kowloon. Stop briefly at Mannings at Mong Kok East Station, buy a bottle of honey and two lemons, and prepare to go home to make lemon honey water.
location: Mannings inside Mong Kok East Station, Kowloon City District, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region

name: Going home, dinner, and parent-child time
description: After arriving home, she put the honey and lemons in the kitchen. Her mother had already prepared dinner, including char siu, stir-fried choy sum, and tomato egg drop soup. The family sat around the table eating, listening to her father talk about an amusing old man he had met while playing chess that day and her son complain that his school math problems were too difficult. After dinner, she helped check her son's Chinese homework and drew a "family portrait" with her daughter using her newly bought crayons.
location: Whampoa Garden Residential Estate, 328 Prince Edward Road West, Kowloon City District, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region

name: Check new hires' progress and have a brief chat.
description: Back in the study, drinking homemade honey lemon water, she opened the company system to check He Junwen's work progress this week. Finding that the client information sorting task was still only about 30 percent done, she sent him a voice message in a calm tone but made the requirements and deadline clear, suggesting he make up the progress on Saturday and that they go over it together on Monday morning.
location: Home study, Whampoa Garden residential estate, 328 Prince Edward Road West, Kowloon City District, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region

name: Personal reflection and relaxation
description: He Junwen's matter was somewhat irritating, so she first sent Su Lishan a WeChat message to inform her of the situation and got her support. Then she briefly complained to her husband Weiming, who had just settled the children down, and he comforted her, saying to take it slow. Afterwards, she stopped dwelling on it, went to wash up, and changed into her pajamas.
location: Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, Kowloon City District, 328 Prince Edward Road West, Whampoa Garden residential estate, study and bedroom at home

name: Reading before bed and getting ready for sleep
description: Leaning against the headboard, I read an e-book recommended by a friend about parent-child communication for a while as a pre-sleep relaxation. Then I set the alarm for 7:00 tomorrow morning (to take my son to play football), turned off my phone, and got ready for bed.
location: Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, Kowloon City District, Whampoa Garden residential estate, 328 Prince Edward Road West, bedroom in the family home

name: Falling asleep
description: After lying down, I recalled the relaxing feeling from today’s yoga class and thought about getting up early tomorrow to be with my son, which made me feel more at ease. Gradually, I drifted off to sleep, recharging for the new day ahead.
location: Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, Kowloon City District, Whampoa Garden residential estate, 328 Prince Edward Road West, bedroom in the family home

name: Morning yoga and body measurement record.
description: The class started on time. The 60-minute restorative session focused on stretching the back of the thighs, hips, and neck and shoulders, with the muscles slowly releasing with each breath. After class, she shared her post-half-marathon feelings with the yoga teacher, who suggested keeping one to two sessions per week. Then she walked home, setting weekly Tuesday and Thursday morning yoga reminders in the calendar on her phone along the way. She sent a WeChat message to her friend Shanshan inviting her to try a yoga class together, and replied to friends' congratulations on her half-marathon results post.
location: Whampoa Garden Residential Estate, 328 Prince Edward Road West, Kowloon City District, Hong Kong.

name: Family breakfast preparation and dining.
description: After yoga, Yu Xiaowei went into the kitchen and brewed a cup of authentic Hong Kong-style milk tea with a strainer. She then helped her mother Chen Meiling prepare breakfast, bringing white congee, shrimp dumplings, and siu mai to the table, and serving small portions for her 8-year-old son Zhang Zixuan and 5-year-old daughter Zhang Yuxin. The family sat around the table enjoying breakfast. While eating, Yu Xiaowei confirmed the day's pick-up and drop-off arrangements with her husband Zhang Weiming: Zhang Weiming would take their son to Kowloon Tsai Sports Ground to play football, and she would later bring their daughter to meet up and take her to the community centre for a painting class, while her mother would handle the afternoon housework and dinner preparation.
location: Whampoa Garden Residential Estate, 328 Prince Edward Road West, Kowloon City District, Hong Kong.

name: Prepared items for going out, and my husband took our son out.
description: After breakfast, Yu Xiaowei and her mother packed up her son's football gear (football shoes, shin guards, and a change of clothes) and her daughter's painting supplies (brushes, paper, and an apron), checked her son's water bottle, and put a pack of cookies into her daughter's backpack. Then she put the dishes and chopsticks into the dishwasher and wiped down the dining table. At 7:45, her husband Zhang Weiming took their son's hand and left, driving to Kowloon Tsai Sports Ground. Yu Xiaowei organized her crossbody bag at the entryway, bringing The Drunkard, a notebook, a power bank, and a water cup, and confirmed that the invitation to the community center book club was saved on her phone.
location: Whampoa Garden Residential Estate, 328 Prince Edward Road West, Kowloon City District, Hong Kong.

name: Drive daughter to Kowloon Tsai Park
description: Yu Xiaowei took her daughter Zhang Yuxin downstairs, drove from Prince Edward Road West, traveled along Argyle Street for about 10 minutes, and arrived at Kowloon Tsai Park at 13 Inverness Road, parking in a metered space near the park.
location: Kowloon Tsai Park, 13 Inverness Road, Kowloon City District, Hong Kong.

name: Walking with my daughter in the park and spending quality time together
description: Yu Xiaowei took her daughter by the hand and strolled along the shaded path in Kowloon Tsai Park. The weather was clear, and sunlight cast dappled shadows through the leaves. The little girl was very interested in the fallen leaves on the ground, so Yu Xiaowei joined her in searching for leaves with special colors and shapes, taking photos with her phone, and promised that when they got home they would use these leaves together with the embroidery materials bought earlier in Sham Shui Po to make an autumn-themed eco-friendly craft.
location: Kowloon Tsai Park, 13 Inverness Road, Kowloon City District, Hong Kong.

name: Pick up son, take daughter to art class, and plan the trip
description: At 10:15, Yu Xiaowei took her daughter early to the exit of Kowloon Tsai Sports Ground to wait for her son Zhang Zixuan. After picking up her sweaty son, she wiped his face and changed him into a dry T-shirt. Then they drove to the Kowloon City Community Centre, about a 10-minute drive. On the way, she listened to her son share fun stories about goals scored in his football class. After arriving at the community centre, Yu Xiaowei took her daughter to the children's painting classroom on the second floor and exchanged a brief greeting with the teacher. Then she sat by the window in the waiting area on the first floor, took out her phone, opened the notes app, and began browsing and collecting itinerary suggestions for a deep tour of Kansai, Japan (Osaka, Kyoto) with her family next year, considering staying in tatami guesthouses, planning to see deer in Nara, and comparing airline prices.
location: Kowloon City Community Centre, Kowloon City District, Hong Kong

name: Picked up her daughter after class and walked home, shopping on the way.
description: After her daughter's class, Yu Xiaowei held her hand and walked home. When they passed the Wellcome supermarket next to the community center, she went in and bought a box of blueberries, which her daughter loved, and a bottle of lemon juice as an extra for lunch.
location: Whampoa Garden Residential Estate, 328 Prince Edward Road West, Kowloon City District, Hong Kong.

name: Family lunch and conversation
description: Back home, her mother Chen Meiling had prepared a sumptuous lunch: steamed grouper, garlic broccoli, and tomato egg drop soup. The whole family sat together eating and chatting. Yu Xiaowei shared her initial ideas for a trip to Kansai; Zhang Weiming and the children showed great interest, and her mother reminded her to be mindful of the budget.
location: Whampoa Garden Residential Estate, 328 Prince Edward Road West, Kowloon City District, Hong Kong.

name: Lunch break, review, and commute to the book club
description: After lunch, Yu Xiaowei first took a 20-minute nap on the bed. Then she went to the study, took out Liu Yichang's The Drunkard, reviewed the underlined sentences and annotations, and focused on the chapters about the conflict between liquor and literary ideals. She wrote down a few keywords she wanted to discuss at the book club. At exactly 14:00, carrying her notebook and the book, she changed into a light cotton-linen long dress and set off on foot from home, walking along Prince Edward Road West for about 10 minutes to Kowloon City Community Centre.
location: Kowloon City Community Centre, Kowloon City District, Hong Kong

name: Participated in the 'One Book a Month' reading club
description: The book club started on time in the activity room on the second floor of the community center, discussing Liu Yichang's The Drunkard. Guided by the moderator, everyone shared their reading impressions in turn. Yu Xiaowei listened carefully. When the discussion turned to "urban alienation," she combined it with her observations from working in Wan Chai and shared her understanding of the protagonist's inner struggle, which won approval from the other readers.
location: Kowloon City Community Centre, Kowloon City District, Hong Kong

name: Connect with fellow readers and build relationships
description: After the book club ended, Yu Xiaowei took the initiative to talk with the retired editor Liang Zhiqiang (Uncle Liang) beside her and full-time mother Chen Meiyi (Ah May). Uncle Liang encouraged her to read more Hong Kong local literature and recommended Chen Hui's Shixiang Ji. Ah May shared her experience of bringing her children to the book club. The three added each other on WeChat and agreed to meet again at next month's book club.
location: Kowloon City Community Centre, Kowloon City District, Hong Kong

name: Walking home, taking a short rest, and recording thoughts from the book club.
description: After saying goodbye to her book friends, Yu Xiaowei walked home. Passing through the community park, she sat on a bench for a while, closed her eyes to feel the evening breeze, and savored the conversation just now. Back home, she went to the study, opened the notes app on her phone, and wrote down the memorable viewpoints and moving passages from the book club. Then she took out The Drunkard from home, reread the opening chapters intensively, and marked new insights with a highlighter.
location: Whampoa Garden Residential Estate, 328 Prince Edward Road West, Kowloon City District, Hong Kong.

name: Family dinner and sharing.
description: Mother had already prepared dinner. After the family sat down, Yu Xiaowei excitedly shared with her husband Zhang Weiming the takeaways from today's book club, recounting her conversation with Uncle Liang, a retired editor, and her new understanding of "The Drunkard." Zhang Weiming appreciated that she had found a new spiritual anchor, and agreed that next time he went to exercise, he could bring a book along.
location: Whampoa Garden Residential Estate, 328 Prince Edward Road West, Kowloon City District, Hong Kong.

name: Parent-child time: drawing tutoring and homework check
description: After the meal, Yu Xiaowei first helped her daughter make a simple collage using the fallen leaves they had picked up today, along with dried flowers and glue from home. Then she went to her son's room, checked his weekend math homework, pointed out the problem-solving approach for several word problems, and encouraged him to redo the calculations himself.
location: Whampoa Garden Residential Estate, 328 Prince Edward Road West, Kowloon City District, Hong Kong.

name: Handle work follow-ups
description: Yu Xiaowei returned to the study and sent a voice message on WeChat to the newcomer He Junwen, reminding him to complete the client file supplementary work they had agreed on last Friday, and telling him that they would go over it together again before Monday morning's meeting.
location: Whampoa Garden Residential Estate, 328 Prince Edward Road West, Kowloon City District, Hong Kong.

name: Couple's leisure time and parent-child reading
description: Yu Xiaowei and Zhang Weiming sat on the sofa together, playfully teasing the family’s orange tabby cat “Afu.” Their daughter came over to share her sticker book. Zhang Weiming scrolled through phone news for a while, while Yu Xiaowei took out the parent-child section of Nonviolent Communication and read for 15 minutes, learning communication skills with children.
location: Whampoa Garden Residential Estate, 328 Prince Edward Road West, Kowloon City District, Hong Kong.

name: Wash up and evening skincare routine.
description: After Yu Xiaowei got the children washed up and settled into bed, she returned to the master bathroom and completed her full evening skincare routine: removing makeup, cleansing, applying essence and face cream, and using a steam eye mask to relax her eyes.
location: Whampoa Garden Residential Estate, 328 Prince Edward Road West, Kowloon City District, Hong Kong.

name: Interacting with the close friends group chat.
description: Wearing a face mask and lying in bed, Yu Xiaowei sent voice messages in the 'Iron Triangle' bestie group chat, excitedly sharing the fun experience of attending her first book club today and chatting with Uncle Liang. Her bestie Lin Jiaxin praised her for having a fulfilling life, while Huang Wenhui curiously asked whether she could join online next time. The three of them chatted about their weekend lives for half an hour.
location: Whampoa Garden Residential Estate, 328 Prince Edward Road West, Kowloon City District, Hong Kong.

name: Couple's bedtime chat and going to sleep.
description: Zhang Weiming finished washing up and got into bed. Yu Xiaowei talked with him about her client schedule for the coming week, mentioning that she had appointments with two clients on Tuesday and Thursday mornings and might need to do a critical illness insurance policy review on Wednesday evening. Zhang Weiming advised her not to overwork herself and suggested taking the children to Sai Kung seaside for a walk on Sunday. After agreeing, they said goodnight. Yu Xiaowei turned off the bedside lamp and soon fell asleep to her husband's steady breathing.
location: Whampoa Garden Residential Estate, 328 Prince Edward Road West, Kowloon City District, Hong Kong.

name: Morning yoga and weigh-in
