Yu Xiaowei barely had an appetite and only scooped a small half bowl of soup to sip slowly. Her husband and parents all noticed she was in a very bad mood. Her husband proactively brought up funny stories about taking the kids skateboarding in the park, and her mother talked about what she wanted to buy at the market tomorrow. She tried to join the conversation, but her eyes were vacant and she often drifted off. After dinner, the kids went to watch TV. She put the dishes in the sink, muttered 'Thanks, Mom,' and walked straight to the study.
location: Home dining room, Whampoa Garden Residential Estate, Kowloon City District, Hong Kong SAR.

name: Made glow-in-the-dark paintings with the children.
description: The children were preparing to make a "creative glow-in-the-dark painting." Yu Xiaowei forced herself to sit between the two children, helping her younger daughter mix colors and demonstrating how to draw the outline of a planet. She mechanically taught her younger daughter how to draw stars, but her mind kept drifting to the matter of the stolen client. After finishing the glow-in-the-dark painting, she turned on her phone flashlight to test the glow effect. The children cheered excitedly, which briefly made her forget her anger, and she gave a bitter smile.
location: Living room/study, Whampoa Garden residential estate, Kowloon City District, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region

name: Alone in the study, processing feelings of betrayal.
description: After putting the children to bed, Yu Xiaowei sat alone under the dim desk lamp. She kept replaying every phone call with Zhou Minyi, confirming that she had never voluntarily disclosed such detailed information about "Mr. Wang" to her. She opened WeChat and looked at their chat history, pausing on the last message "Good night," unable to move for a long time. Anger, disappointment, and humiliation intertwined, making her chest feel tight. She tried to read through her CFP notes, but couldn't take in a single word. In the end, she closed the book, tears welling up in her eyes.
location: Study, Whampoa Garden residential estate, Kowloon City District, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region

name: The agony of insomnia.
description: Yu Xiaowei quietly turned off the study light, lay down on the bed, and tossed and turned. The moonlight outside the window shone coldly into the room, while the name “Min Yi” and the client's face kept recurring in her mind. She stayed awake all night, and only when the sky outside began to brighten did she manage to doze off briefly out of sheer exhaustion.
location: Master bedroom, Whampoa Garden residential estate, Kowloon City District, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region

name: Pre-race tapering easy run and stretching.
description: Even though you slept less than 3 hours last night due to insomnia, you still got up decisively when the 5:50 alarm rang. After a quick wash-up, you put on running shoes and walked 12 minutes to Kowloon Tsai Park. Following coach Zhao Zhiming's tapering plan, you did an 8 km easy run, monitored by a heart rate strap, keeping a steady pace of 6:40/km. After the run, you did 10 minutes of stretching on a park bench, took a photo of the track in the morning light, and checked in by sending it to your coach.
location: Kowloon Tsai Park, 13 Inverness Road, Kowloon City District, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, China

name: Returned home for a shower and family breakfast.
description: After the morning run, I walked home, took a shower, and changed into comfortable loungewear. I had breakfast with my family who had just gotten up; my mother had prepared Hong Kong-style wonton noodles. While eating, I asked the children about their plans for the day. My son Xuanxuan shouted that he wanted to play soccer in the afternoon, while my daughter Xinxin wanted to draw. I smiled and agreed, and suggested going out together in the afternoon.
location: Hong Kong Special Administrative Region of China, Kowloon City District, 328 Prince Edward Road West, Whampoa Garden residential estate

name: Handling Mid-Autumn Festival dinner matters and family contact
description: After breakfast, you moved to the study to handle the Mid-Autumn dinner. First, you called your mother to confirm the menu and number of guests she had planned. Next, you messaged your younger brother Yu Xiaofeng on WhatsApp to confirm the exact time his family would be returning from Shenzhen to Hong Kong. Finally, you summoned the courage to call your father, Yu Guoqiang, and asked lightly whether he could come to the Mid-Autumn dinner. He still vaguely made excuses, saying he had “things to do.” You felt a pang of disappointment but did not say much, simply telling him to take care of himself before hanging up.
location: Home study, Whampoa Garden Residential Estate, 328 Prince Edward Road West, Kowloon City District, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, China.

name: Officially reserve the Mid-Autumn Festival dinner
description: After hanging up with your father, you calmed yourself down. Taking out your phone and searching your contacts, you called Fuling Restaurant in Kowloon City, a regular place you often went to (address: 181 Prince Edward Road West, Kowloon City, about a 10-minute walk from home), to book a private room seating 10 for Mid-Autumn Festival evening. You confirmed the time and number of guests (you, your husband, two children, your mother, and your younger brother's family of three), and wrote down the reservation number.
location: Home study, Whampoa Garden Residential Estate, 328 Prince Edward Road West, Kowloon City District, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, China.

name: Forcing myself to stay sharp to review CFP portfolio theory
description: You returned to your desk, opened the CFP course app, and focused on reviewing the 'Portfolio Theory' chapter. You forced yourself to concentrate, studied concepts such as the diversification effect and the efficient frontier, and tried to create a mind map using XMind software. Because you were sleepy, you were not very efficient, but you still persisted and completed a 30-minute mock test. There were many wrong answers. You sighed and marked in your mistake notebook: 'Focus on conquering the portfolio section next week.' During the break, you went downstairs to the convenience store in the community and bought a bottle of sugar-free cola to refresh yourself.
location: Home study, Whampoa Garden Residential Estate, 328 Prince Edward Road West, Kowloon City District, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, China.

name: Light family lunch
description: At lunchtime, Mother made steamed sea bass, blanched choy sum, and brown rice — very light and healthy. You praised Mother's cooking and chatted with your husband Zhang Weiming, mentioning how Father avoids the Mid-Autumn reunion dinner. Weiming comforted you not to rush, and suggested that before the Mid-Autumn Festival he would go with you to invite Father for dim sum. You nodded in agreement, feeling somewhat relieved.
location: Dining room at home, Whampoa Garden residential estate, 328 Prince Edward Road West, Kowloon City District, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, China

name: Midday nap and relaxation
description: After the meal, you felt both physically and mentally exhausted. You lay on the bed with your eyes closed and rested for 20 minutes. You tried a 5-minute meditation to let your tense nerves relax a little.
location: Bedroom at home, Whampoa Garden Residential Estate, 328 Prince Edward Road West, Kowloon City District, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, China

name: New Cantonese embroidery work "Daughter's World Autumn" launched
description: At 2 p.m., you sit down at the Cantonese embroidery worktable. You pull up a photo on your phone of your daughter's back under the ginkgo tree in Kowloon Tsai Park last autumn as inspiration. After carefully selecting gold, orange, and brown silk threads, you use a water-soluble pen to sketch the rough outline on white satin. Your 5-year-old daughter Xinxin runs in curiously, and you patiently teach her to identify the colors of the silk threads; she excitedly helps you pass the scissors. After she leaves, you begin to make the first stitch in earnest. As the needle and thread move, your emotions gradually settle down from the insomnia and the matter with your father, and you gain a moment of inner peace.
location: Cantonese embroidery work area at home, Whampoa Garden Residential Estate, 328 Prince Edward Road West, Kowloon City District, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, China.

name: Getting ready to go out for a walk with her husband.
description: You pack up the embroidery frame and change into casual going-out clothes. You call your husband Zhang Weiming and say, "Weiming, let's go out for a walk while we have the chance." He puts down his phone and happily agrees.
location: Hong Kong Special Administrative Region of China, Kowloon City District, 328 Prince Edward Road West, Whampoa Garden residential estate

name: Walking and talking with her husband outside Mong Kok Stadium.
description: Starting from home, you walked along Prince Edward Road West for about 13 minutes, passing through quiet streets, and came to the path around Mong Kok Grand Stadium for a walk. The autumn breeze brushed gently, and you told him the root of your insomnia last night - being robbed of a client by your best friend Zhou Minyi, setbacks in training, and your father's absence at Mid-Autumn Festival, one after another weighing on your mind. Weiming listened quietly, then held your hand and said steadily: "Xiaowei, we'll figure out a way together to make up for the client issue this Saturday and Sunday, and I'll help you arrange a meeting with your father. Don't carry it alone." His words made your tense shoulders relax.
location: Outside Mong Kok Stadium, 37 Flower Market Road, Kowloon City District, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, China

name: Picked up the kids, went shopping together, and collected mall rewards.
description: After the walk, you picked up the children, who were playing on the slide downstairs, on the way. Xuanxuan suddenly wanted mangoes, so you suggested going to Kowloon City Market to buy some fresh fruit. The family of four walked about 20 minutes to the market and chose Thai mangoes, dragon fruit, and kiwi fruit. Then you walked about 13 minutes to Whampoa New World shopping mall, where the children each picked a box of building blocks at the toy store as a reward for behaving well this week.
location: Kowloon City Market, 102 Nga Tsin Wai Road, Kowloon City District, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, and Whampoa New World Shopping Mall, 6 Tak Hong Street

name: Family parent-child building block time
description: After returning home, you and the children play with the newly bought building blocks on the carpet. Xuanxuan builds a racing car, while Xinxin builds a little castle and proudly shows it to you. Weiming is in the kitchen helping his mother prepare dinner.
location: Home living room, Whampoa Garden Residential Estate, 328 Prince Edward Road West, Kowloon City District, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, China

name: Warm family dinner
description: Mother made your favorite green radish and carrot pork bone soup, along with white-cut chicken and garlic stir-fried choy sum. At the dinner table, everyone talked about the funny things that happened today. Xinxin showed off her "castle", while Xuanxuan excitedly said he was going to be the captain in next week's soccer match. The warm, harmonious atmosphere eased your daytime worries.
location: Dining room at home, Whampoa Garden residential estate, 328 Prince Edward Road West, Kowloon City District, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, China

name: Evening personal tidying and core relaxation
description: After the meal, you returned to the study. First, you wrote in your diary, recording today's feelings about your father and the experience of walking with Weiming. Then you opened the memo app on your phone and listed the client follow-up items to handle next Monday (specially marked "the issue with Mr. Wang requires a remediation plan"). Next, you unrolled a yoga mat on the floor and did a 15-minute home core workout and stretching to relax the muscles tightened by the morning run and recent stress.
location: Study and living room at home, Whampoa Garden residential estate, 328 Prince Edward Road West, Kowloon City District, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, China.

name: Preparing tomorrow's tasks and bedtime routine
description: You took a hot shower and changed into pajamas. You carefully relaxed the gastrocnemius and quadriceps of your right leg with a fascia gun, and applied soothing cream to your calves. You checked your phone to make sure the alarm for tomorrow (Monday) at 6:30 a.m. was set, and confirmed the work badge and client materials bag to bring to work tomorrow.
location: Bedroom and bathroom at home, Whampoa Garden residential estate, 328 Prince Edward Road West, Kowloon City District, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region of China

name: Reading and bedtime
description: You lie in bed and flip through a few pages of The Illustrated Guide to Basic Cantonese Embroidery Stitches, which you hadn't finished reading, until drowsiness sets in. You turn off the bedside lamp, say goodnight to Weiming beside you, then close your eyes and try to calm yourself into sleep.
location: Bedroom at home, Whampoa Garden Residential Estate, 328 Prince Edward Road West, Kowloon City District, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, China

name: Waking up and morning stretching and meditation
description: After her 7:30 AM alarm went off, Yu Xiaowei got up and weighed herself: 53.5 kg. She laid a yoga mat on the bedroom floor and did 15 minutes of stretching and meditation, focusing on relaxing her right leg. With her father's matter weighing on her mind, she tried to calm down through meditation and gather energy for the new day.
location: Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, Kowloon City District, 328 Prince Edward Road West, home master bedroom

name: Had breakfast with family.
description: After washing up, Yu Xiaowei walked into the dining room. Her mother, Chen Meiling, had prepared plain congee, shrimp dumplings, siu mai, BBQ pork buns, and Hong Kong-style milk tea. She strictly controlled her diet, eating only half a bowl of congee and one shrimp dumpling, and taking a few sips of milk tea. Her son Zhang Zixuan excitedly talked about a lantern he had dreamed of, while her daughter Zhang Yuxin quietly drank her congee. Her husband Zhang Weiming asked about the time for making lanterns in the afternoon, and she tried to keep smiling as she responded.
location: Dining room at home, 328 Prince Edward Road West, Kowloon City District, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region

name: Morning: CFP investment portfolio theory study
description: After breakfast, Yu Xiaowei returned to her study, spread out the CFP portfolio theory mind map, and used a red pen to mark the difficult points of 'Capital Asset Pricing Model' and 'Efficient Market Hypothesis'. She copied the key formulas onto sticky notes, photographed the wrong questions and sent them to the study group. Then, starting at 9 o'clock, she focused on reviewing, sorting out the mind map, repeatedly deducing the formulas, clarifying the logic of the wrong questions, completing 20 key practice questions, and organizing the wrong-question explanations to share in the study group. She felt she had gained a lot.
location: Study at home, 328 Prince Edward Road West, Kowloon City District, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region

name: Checked her son's holiday homework.
description: Yu Xiaowei came out of the study and saw her mother preparing the soup base for lunch. She called her son Zhang Zixuan over to check his holiday homework and found careless calculation errors in the steps of two word problems on the math test paper. She patiently guided him to reorganize his thinking until he understood.
location: Living room at home, 328 Prince Edward Road West, Kowloon City District, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region

name: Light family lunch
description: Her mother Chen Meiling made pork bone soup with green radish and carrot, served with stir-fried broccoli and steamed grass carp. Yu Xiaowei had a bowl of soup, ate fish and vegetables, and strictly controlled her carbohydrate intake. During the meal, she reminded everyone about the dinner at Fu Lin Seafood Restaurant in the evening and asked them to save room. Her husband Zhang Weiming planned to take the children for a walk near Hung Hom Pier in the afternoon.
location: Dining room at home, 328 Prince Edward Road West, Kowloon City District, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region

name: Midday break and emotional processing
description: After the meal, Yu Xiaowei went back to the bedroom, drew the curtains, and lay down, but her thoughts were hard to calm. She checked the chat history with her father again; there was still no new message. She forced herself to rest and eventually slept for about half an hour. The alarm woke her up, saving energy for the afternoon's activities.
location: Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, Kowloon City District, 328 Prince Edward Road West, home master bedroom

name: Making Mid-Autumn Festival lanterns with the children and preparing the materials
description: After the midday rest, Yu Xiaowei took out colored paper, bamboo strips, scissors, glue, markers, and small bells from the storage cabinet, placed them on the living room coffee table, and bagged the homemade double-yolk white lotus seed paste mooncakes. In the afternoon, after Zhang Zixuan and Zhang Yuxin returned from the park, the three sat around and made lanterns. The daughter drew a rabbit, the son cut out stars and the moon, and Yu Xiaowei bent bamboo strips to make the frame. When the lantern was finally finished, they tied on the bell, and her son wrote the words 'reunion' on it, then hung it in the living room, filling the home with a festive atmosphere.
location: Living room at home, 328 Prince Edward Road West, Kowloon City District, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region

name: Afternoon preparation and departure for the dinner gathering.
description: After finishing the lantern, Yu Xiaowei tidied up the remaining materials and returned to the bedroom to change into a wine-red knit dress. She applied light makeup to cover her dark circles and practiced smiling in front of the mirror. Then she went downstairs alone and strolled along the streets of Hung Hom, walking to the fresh food store on the first floor of The Whampoa mall to buy a box of Kyoho grapes. She then returned home, where her husband had already helped the children change clothes. Her daughter was still holding the lantern she had just made, and her mother had put on a dark red patterned top. Yu Xiaowei checked the mooncakes and grapes, and the whole family walked cheerfully to Fulin Fish Harbour on Ming On Street, seeing other children playing with lanterns along the way.
location: 328 Prince Edward Road West, Kowloon City District, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, and along the way to Fu Lam Fisherman's Wharf on Ming On Street

name: Mid-Autumn Family Dinner at Fu Lin Fishing Harbour
description: The whole family arrived at the private room of Fulin Fishing Harbour (Hung Hom branch). Her younger brother Yu Xiaofeng had already arrived and confirmed the menu with the waiter. Yu Xiaowei asked the waiter to serve hot tea, put the homemade mooncakes and bought grapes on the table, and hung the lanterns she made in the afternoon in the corner of the private room as decoration. During the meal, she tried hard to liven up the atmosphere, picked up food for the children, clinked glasses with her brother, and even made an exception to taste half a lotus seed paste mooncake. Her mother smiled from ear to ear, and the children were excited. She secretly sent a text message to her father, telling him she had packed his favorite char siu bao, but he did not reply.
location: Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, Kowloon City District, Ming On Street, Fulum Fishery Harbour (Hung Hom Branch)

name: Younger brother privately questioned father's absence
description: As the family dinner was drawing to an end, her younger brother Yu Xiaofeng made an excuse to go downstairs for some fresh air and pulled Yu Xiaowei over to the flower bed beside the restaurant. He lowered his voice and demanded, "Sis, what exactly are you going to do about Dad? He didn't even come today on Mid-Autumn Festival. It's been over half a year. Are you afraid of hurting his pride, or are you afraid that airing the family's dirty laundry will affect your insurance business?" Yu Xiaowei was stung by his sharp words. Suppressed grievances and helplessness surged up, and she almost burst into tears. She could only reply quietly, "Do you think... I still have a way?" and fell silent.
location: By the flower bed near Fulin Fish Harbor (Hung Hom Branch) on Ming On Street, Kowloon City District, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region

name: After calming herself down alone, she went home and had a late-night talk with her husband.
description: Yu Xiaowei asked her husband to take the family home first, then walked alone aimlessly along the streets of Hung Hom for about 15 minutes and sat down on a quiet bench near Kun Yam Street. Gazing at the full moon, she sent her father a Mid-Autumn Festival greeting message, and also texted her younger brother saying she would find a way and asked for more time. Tears silently fell. Afterward, she composed herself and walked home. When she arrived, her husband was waiting for her in the living room and gave her a quiet hug. Leaning on his shoulder, she said she had been avoiding facing her father's problem and decided to go talk to him in person. Her husband promised to go with her.
location: Home, Hung Hom Street, near Kwun Yam Street and 328 Prince Edward Road West, Kowloon City District, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region

name: With her husband, soothed the children to sleep and told the Mid-Autumn Festival legend.
description: Yu Xiaowei and her husband changed the children into pajamas. Her daughter Zhang Yuxin, holding the lantern she had made in the afternoon, insisted on telling a story about the moon. Yu Xiaowei sat by the bed and softly told the legend of Chang'e flying to the moon. The two children listened attentively and quickly fell asleep. Then she and her husband returned to the master bedroom, briefly discussed plans for the next day, and her husband said he would take leave to accompany them.
location: Children's room and master bedroom, 328 Prince Edward Road West, Kowloon City District, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region

name: Evening personal care, journaling, and reading before bed.
description: In the bathroom, Yu Xiaowei used a fascia gun to relax her stiff right leg and completed her evening skincare routine. Then she went to the study to write in her diary, recording the day's mood and reflections, pondering her younger brother's questioning, and deciding to go to To Kwa Wan the next day to talk with her father face to face. In the diary she also wrote her post-holiday work plan: follow up on client Wang's proposal and arrange client Ah Shen's policy annual review. Afterwards, she returned to the bedroom, lay on the bed, and flipped through the 'Illustrated Guide to Basic Cantonese Embroidery Stitches'. The concentration brought her calm. At 11 p.m., she turned off the light, listened to the laughter and wind outside the window, and gradually fell asleep.
location: Bathroom, study, and master bedroom at home, 328 Prince Edward Road West, Kowloon City District, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region

name: Wake up, morning meditation and stretching
description: Woke up in the soft morning light and the patter of fine rain outside the window, first doing breathing meditation in bed to calm the mind. Then got up, walked to the balcony, and did simple yoga stretches facing the wet street to awaken the body and relieve tension in the shoulders and neck.
location: Master bedroom and balcony, Whampoa Garden residential estate, 328 Prince Edward Road West, Kowloon City District, Hong Kong

name: Prepare breakfast, chat with mother, and enjoy breakfast
description: After changing into loungewear, she went into the kitchen and prepared breakfast with her mother, cutting fruit and brewing pu'er tea, softly talking about her father's absence at last night's Mid-Autumn Festival dinner, with a plaintive tone. Her mother comforted her, saying her father had the family in his heart. Then the whole family sat around and enjoyed breakfast, drinking plain congee, eating rice noodle rolls and honeydew melon. Under the table, her husband gently squeezed her hand. Her son complained about not wanting to go to school, and her daughter obediently ate her egg. She reminded the children to do their homework after school.
location: Kitchen and dining room, Whampoa Garden residence, Kowloon City District, Hong Kong

name: Take the children to school and return home
description: Her husband drove, and together they took the children to school. First they drove along Prince Edward Road West and Waterloo Road to Kowloon Tong Government Primary School to drop off their son, then along Boundary Street and Argyle Street to Kowloon City Kindergarten to take their daughter to school. After that they returned home to Whampoa Garden. In the car, she confirmed with her husband the plan to visit her father in To Kwa Wan in the afternoon. Her husband suggested calling first to confirm where her father was, thinking it would be safer.
location: Kowloon City District, Hong Kong, passing Kowloon Tong Government Primary School (Cumberland Road, Kowloon Tong) and Kowloon City Kindergarten (206 Argyle Street, Ma Tau Wai), then returning to Whampoa Garden.

name: Focused on CFP study (behavioral finance chapter)
description: She brewed a cup of Pu'er tea for herself, sat down at the desk in the study, and opened her laptop to study the behavioral finance chapter of the CFP textbook. She listened to a recorded online lecture while taking careful notes. When the lecture covered investment biases such as overconfidence and loss aversion, she thought of her father's stubbornness with stocks and her mother's risk aversion, and wrote her reflections in the margins of her notes. After finishing the chapter, she started on the accompanying practice questions.
location: Study of the residence at Whampoa Garden, Kowloon City District, Hong Kong

name: Short break, stretching and meditation, and preparing lunch with her mother.
description: After finishing the intensive study session, she got up to move around, opened the living room window for fresh air, and followed a mobile app for shoulder and neck stretches and core activation. Then she closed her eyes and did mindful meditation, focusing on her breath and temporarily setting aside her emotions about her father. Afterward she went into the kitchen, where her mother was preparing lunch: steamed chicken breast, blanched broccoli, and tomato egg drop soup. She helped set the table. Her husband also came home from work, and the family of three ate and chatted, sharing insights from the morning's study of behavioral finance. When she mentioned the anchoring effect, her husband joked that her father was exactly that—anchored by stock prices.
location: Living room, kitchen, and dining room of the Whampoa Garden residence in Kowloon City District, Hong Kong

name: Lunch break, organizing CFP notes, and preparing talking points
description: After lunch, she felt tired and took a 20-minute nap on the living room sofa. After waking, she called her father and said in a calm tone that she and her husband would go over to see him in the afternoon. After a silence, he agreed. After hanging up, she returned to her study and wrote a brief learning reflection combining the morning's behavioral finance content with her father's situation and her own client cases, marking concepts such as confirmation bias and disposition effect for further understanding. At the same time, she wrote down the key points of the conversation with her father in her diary so that she could stay calm in the afternoon.
location: You can reply like this: 'Mr. Wang, thank you for the invitation! I'm very interested in the Shenzhen cross-border insurance market. Could you let me know the general agenda of the sharing session and who will be attending? I can prepare cases in advance that match mainland clients' needs. Also, should I prepare bilingual materials?' This shows enthusiasm and also makes you seem thorough and professional.

name: Changing clothes and heading to father's house
description: After changing into a neat casual outfit (dark blue knit top, khaki casual pants, and flats), picking up her bag, and taking a box of double-yolk white lotus paste mooncakes from Kee Wah Bakery as a gift, she and her husband, who had also changed, drove off together along To Kwa Wan Road toward To Kwa Wan. They were silent on the way, each mentally organizing what to say. Around 15:00, the car stopped at the foot of the old tenement building where her father lived.
location: From Whampoa Garden in Kowloon City District, Hong Kong, along To Kwa Wan Road to the downstairs of father Yu Guoqiang's home at 28 Mei King Street, To Kwa Wan

name: Formal Communication with Father
description: Went upstairs and knocked on the door. When her father opened it, the room was dim and smelled of smoke. She walked into the living room and sat down, first chatting about family matters and handing over the mooncakes. Then she took a deep breath, held her husband's hand, and gathered the courage to say: "Dad, you didn't come for the Mid-Autumn Festival last night. Mom misses you very much, and we're all worried about you." Her father lowered his head and remained silent. She then continued softly, talking about his previous investment losses and saying that she didn't mean to blame him—she was just afraid that if he kept dwelling on it and avoiding the family, he would truly be the one who had lost himself. Her husband also chimed in, saying that the most important thing for a family is to be united. Her father's eyes reddened. After a long silence, he said hoarsely, "I know I messed up. I didn't want it to be this way." The moment those words were spoken, the heavy stone on her chest suddenly felt lighter. Although they didn't go into details, what mattered was that the conversation had begun.
location: At the home of her father, Yu Guoqiang, 28 Mei King Street, To Kwa Wan, Kowloon City District, Hong Kong

name: Returned and picked up the children from school
description: After leaving her father's house, she let out a long sigh of relief, feeling an ease she hadn't felt in a long time. On the drive home, she chatted casually with her husband about the plans for the evening. They first dropped by Kowloon City Kindergarten to pick up their daughter, then went to Kowloon Tong Government Primary School to pick up their son. The children were especially happy to see both Mom and Dad coming to pick them up. In the car, she told the children about visiting Grandpa that afternoon, saying he admitted he had been a bit stubborn and would attend more family gatherings in the future. The children were glad to hear that Grandpa was fine.
location: Returned from To Kwa Wan, passing by Kowloon City Kindergarten (206 Argyle Street, Ma Tau Wai) and Kowloon Tong Government Primary School (Cumberland Road, Kowloon Tong), and went back to Whampoa Garden.

name: Warm family time, helping with dinner, and dinner with the whole family
description: After returning home, she changed into home clothes and helped her daughter build a little castle with LEGO bricks, while her son read comics nearby. Then she went to the kitchen to help her mother peel garlic and trim vegetables, and told her happily, "Mom, I talked things through with Dad. He himself admitted that he was just being too proud." Her mother's eyes reddened at the words and she said good repeatedly. For dinner, her mother made steamed fish, stir-fried choy sum, and shrimp with scrambled eggs. The atmosphere was relaxed, and she had a better appetite, eating half a bowl more rice. At the table, she encouraged her son to call his grandfather to say hello, and shared the little behavioral finance knowledge she had learned that day. Her husband raised his teacup and toasted her with tea instead of wine, and she felt warm inside.
location: Living room, kitchen, and dining room of the Whampoa Garden residence in Kowloon City District, Hong Kong

name: Brushed the pet cat Bailey's fur.
description: After dinner, feeling relaxed in body and mind, I took out the dedicated grooming brush from the utility cabinet and called the pet cat Bailey. Bailey walked over with elegant cat steps and rubbed against my leg. My daughter also ran over to help. I sat down on the carpet and gently brushed Bailey's long fur, humming a tune. Bailey purred comfortably while my daughter fed it small treats. This warm moment made all stress and worries temporarily disappear.
location: On the carpet in the living room of Whampoa Garden residence, Kowloon City District, Hong Kong

name: Tutoring children with homework and parent-child reading
description: She first went to the study and called her son over, checked his math homework, and explained a few wrong problems to him. Then she went to her daughter’s room and read a picture book about a little rabbit with her, telling the story once in Cantonese and once in Mandarin. Seeing the children’s focused and satisfied expressions, she felt the happiness of being a mother.
location: Home study and daughter's room at Whampoa Garden, Kowloon City District, Hong Kong

name: Home strength training
description: Changed into a sports tank top and leggings, and laid out the yoga mat in the living room. Followed the mobile app to complete a 15-minute strength training session: 3 sets of 15 squats, 3 sets of 12 lunges per side, 3 sets of 15 glute bridges, and 30 seconds of side plank per side. After the workout, used a massage gun to carefully relax the front and back thigh muscles, and felt the legs much looser.
location: Living room of Whampoa Garden residence, Kowloon City District, Hong Kong.

name: Shower, evening skincare routine, and journaling.
description: After training, I took a comfortable hot shower, applied a hydrating face mask, sat down at my desk, opened my diary, and recorded this extraordinary day: I mustered the courage to talk to my father, and he admitted he was wrong, so a weight was lifted from my mind. In the evening, while grooming Beili, I felt that my family was doing well, and I was very happy. After finishing the diary, I planned the post-holiday work list for the next few days.
location: Bedroom and bathroom of the residence at Whampoa Garden, Kowloon City District, Hong Kong

name: Reading and preparation before bed
description: Lying in bed, she picked up the 'Illustrated Guide to Basic Cantonese Embroidery Stitches' and read for 20 minutes, studying a few new stitches. Then she set the alarm for 6:30 the next morning, confirmed the list of clients she needed to contact, turned off her phone, said goodnight to her husband beside her, and fell into a deep, peaceful sleep.
location: Bedroom in the Whampoa Garden residence, Kowloon City District, Hong Kong

name: Morning family time and farewell.
description: I woke up at 8:15, lay in bed for two minutes, and recalled the warm moments of reconciliation with my father Yu Guoqiang yesterday. After getting up, I washed up briefly and changed into yoga clothes. When I walked out of the bedroom, my husband Zhang Weiming had already prepared breakfast—Hong Kong-style milk tea and whole wheat toast—and he told me to focus on studying today. The children had already finished breakfast. I kissed my son Xuanxuan (8 years old) and my daughter Xinxin (5 years old) on the foreheads and wished them a happy day at school. At 9 o'clock sharp, my husband took the children out. He was responsible for taking Xuanxuan to the school bus stop in the residential area, then riding a bicycle to take Xinxin to Kowloon City Kindergarten.
location: Bedroom and dining room at home, Whampoa Garden residential estate, 328 Prince Edward Road West, Kowloon City District, Hong Kong.

name: Morning CFP study and quiz
description: After seeing the family off, the house became quiet. She first opened the window in the study to ventilate, and poured some cat food for the cat Bailey. She took out her CFP study notebook and textbooks, set her phone to Do Not Disturb mode, keeping only the course app and timer, and prepared to enter a study state. At 9:20, she began studying the asset allocation principles chapter using the CFP course app, listening to the audio explanation of the relationship between risk and return and the characteristics of different asset classes while drawing charts in her notebook and recording key concepts. During the process, she proactively paused to apply the theory to past client cases she had handled. At 11:20, she opened the chapter quiz in the app. Of 20 questions, she got 2 wrong, a score of 88%. She immediately screenshotted the wrong questions and wrote down the corresponding knowledge points and correct explanations in red pen to ensure full mastery. After studying, she got up, went to the balcony to stretch and relax her neck and shoulders, then went to the kitchen to prepare lunch.
location: Study and balcony, Whampoa Garden, 328 Prince Edward Road West, Kowloon City District, Hong Kong

name: Lunch and lunch break.
description: She opened the fridge, took out the chicken breast and broccoli that her mother Chen Meiling had helped buy yesterday, and prepared a simple meal of blanched broccoli and pan-seared chicken breast for herself (today is the 8th day of the diet control plan). Starting at 12 o'clock, she enjoyed lunch alone in the dining room: chicken breast with olive oil and a little black pepper, broccoli, and a small bowl of rice, while replying to several client WhatsApp messages on her phone. After eating, she leaned back on the sofa and rested with her eyes closed for 10 minutes to refresh herself before the afternoon study session.
location: Kitchen and dining room, Whampoa Garden residential estate, 328 Prince Edward Road West, Kowloon City District, Hong Kong

name: Midday Yin Yoga and Meditation
description: At 12:50 she changed into a sports vest and yoga pants, picked up her yoga mat, and walked three minutes to Whampoa Fitness Centre (60 m southeast of the intersection of Hung Lun Road and Oi King Street). At exactly 1 p.m., in the quiet yoga studio, Instructor Lin taught breathing techniques and then led a 40-minute yin yoga practice focused on stretching the hips, lower back, shoulders and neck. In 'Pigeon Pose' and 'Butterfly Pose' she closed her eyes and matched deep, long breaths, imagining herself on the hilltop at Kowloon Tsai Park feeling the breeze, letting go of the frustration from the recent trail training and the tension from studying bit by bit. Afterwards, Instructor Lin guided a 5-minute seated meditation. At 1:50 p.m. she walked home, drank half a glass of warm water, put away her yoga mat, and sat quietly on the sofa to stay calm.
location: Whampoa Fitness Centre, 60 meters southeast of the intersection of Hung Luen Road and Oi King Street, Kowloon City District, Hong Kong

name: Afternoon CFP study and review
description: She sat back down at the desk, refreshed and energized, and started the afternoon study session, focusing on the asset allocation strategy section (strategic and tactical asset allocation). Using the mind map feature in a mobile app, she linked the morning and afternoon content into a knowledge framework. Outside, the sky cleared and sunlight streamed through the blinds onto the desk. After finishing the lesson at 3:30 p.m., she took out the wrong questions from the morning and the unclear concepts from the afternoon exercises, and made a one-page review sheet titled 'Asset Allocation Principles One-Page Review Notes', marking key points and common mistakes with different colored highlighters. When it was done, she took a photo and planned to share it with friends in the exam preparation group.
location: Hong Kong, Kowloon City District, 328 Prince Edward Road West, Whampoa Garden residential estate, study room

name: Afternoon outing: market shopping and pet store
description: At 16:00, she changed into going-out clothes, put on a sun hat, and left, walking along Prince Edward Road West for about 15 minutes to the bustling Prince Edward Road West street market. First, at the time-honored Jinhua Bakery, she bought two freshly baked egg tarts as an afternoon tea treat for herself, then browsed as she picked out fresh salmon and vegetables, planning to make dinner for the family. At 16:40, on the way home, she turned into Furry Kid Pet Shop on Prince Edward Road West near the Boundary Street section, and picked out a bag of her cat Bailey's favorite chicken-flavored freeze-dried treats. Then she walked back home to Whampoa Garden carrying the ingredients and cat treats.
location: Prince Edward Road West Market, Prince Edward Road West, Kowloon City District, Hong Kong; passing by Maohaizi Pet Shop on Prince Edward Road West near Boundary Street.

name: Picking up the children and family dinner
description: I got home at 17:15. My mother, Chen Meiling, was already trimming vegetables, so I put down my things, washed my hands, and helped. At 17:45, my mother and I walked to the community school bus stop to pick up my son Xuanxuan, who had come back on the school bus. Then we walked together to Kowloon City Kindergarten (206 Argyle Street, Ma Tau Wai) to pick up my daughter Xinxin, arriving at 17:55. After picking up the children, we walked home and arrived at about 18:15. After my husband Zhang Weiming got off work, the family sat around the dining table and enjoyed dinner: blanched shrimp, steamed salmon, garlic broccoli, and pork bone soup with choy sum. During the meal, I shared what I had learned, and Xinxin said she had drawn a picture about clouds and sheep at kindergarten today. The whole family was happy and harmonious.
location: School bus stop at Whampoa Garden estate, Kowloon City Kindergarten (206 Argyle Street, Ma Tau Wai), home dining room at Whampoa Garden residential estate, 328 Prince Edward Road West, Kowloon City District, Hong Kong

name: Evening chores, feeding the cat, and parent-child time

At 7:30 p.m., I first tutored my son Xuanxuan on his math homework in the study, patiently explaining the wrong questions; then my daughter Xinxin took out her watercolor sketchbook and said she wanted to learn embroidery, so I took out my unfinished Cantonese embroidery piece Autumn in My Daughter's World and taught her on the living room coffee table, hand in hand, how to embroider the outline of a small flower with flat stitches. Xinxin learned seriously and happily.
location: Living room, kitchen, and study at Whampoa Garden residential estate, 328 Prince Edward Road West, Kowloon City District, Hong Kong

name: Evening stretching and video chat with running buddy

At 9:00 p.m. sharp I connected a video call with my running buddy Shen Peiwen, and we each did a 30-minute stretching session at home in sync. Shen Peiwen smiled and asked how my studies were going, then comforted me in an optimistic tone: "What's a failed training run? I had a run fall apart last time too. The important thing is that we can learn from it—just focus on the next phase!" Her words reignited my confidence in running.
location: Living room at Whampoa Garden residential estate, 328 Prince Edward Road West, Kowloon City District, Hong Kong

name: Bedtime routine: wash up, podcast, late-night chat, and sleep.
description: After the video call ended, I took a hot shower, changed into comfortable pajamas, sat at the dressing table applying night cream, and combed my hair with a wooden comb. Then I took out my diary and jotted down today's reflections: study goals met, yoga relaxation, mood improved after talking with Shen Peiwen. At 10 p.m., I put on my Bluetooth earbuds and opened the podcast app, listening to the Kowloon Walled City special episode of the podcast Left and Right recommended by my best friend Huang Wenhui to learn about the history of the Walled City. I was so absorbed that I paused after more than 20 minutes, planning to continue tomorrow morning. At 10:25 p.m., my husband Zhang Weiming got into bed. I took off my earbuds and shared my study achievements and funny bits from the podcast. We chatted for a while, then I set the alarm for the next workday and confirmed the documents to bring to work and my commuting route. At 10:35 p.m., we said goodnight, turned off the lamp, sank into the soft mattress, and soon fell into a peaceful sleep.
location: Bedroom and bathroom, Whampoa Garden residential estate, 328 Prince Edward Road West, Kowloon City District, Hong Kong

After breakfast, her husband took their daughter to kindergarten, while she accompanied her son downstairs to wait for the school bus and told him to come straight home after school. One old client's renewal inquiry required calculating the premium, so I made notes in the system and planned to communicate with Guo Junwei from the actuarial department next week.

Yu Xiaowei proactively reported today's plan to win back the Shenzhen client, earning a nod of approval and encouragement from Liang Zhenhua.

name: Late-night insomnia and a long husband-wife talk
description: Lying in bed, Yu Xiaowei tossed and turned, unable to sleep, as images of her colleague Zhou Minyi snatching the client and her father's stubborn figure played over and over in her mind. Her husband Zhang Weiming noticed she was not herself, got up and went to the kitchen to make two cups of hot milk, handed one to her, then sat on the edge of the bed and asked softly, “Is there something you’re keeping from me?” Yu Xiaowei finally let down her guard and poured out everything about losing the client, the pressure at work, and her father’s stubborn investment. Zhang Weiming held her hand and said gently but firmly, “No matter how hard things are outside, there will always be someone at home supporting you. We are a family; there is no hurdle we can’t get over.” They talked until 2 a.m., and for the first time in a long while, Yu Xiaowei felt reassured and relaxed, and finally fell into a deep sleep.

I jogged 200 meters between sets to recover. After the run, I stretched carefully for 15 minutes and used a massage gun to focus on releasing my calves and quadriceps. Her daughter became nervous when she saw a group of little girls wearing the same dance costumes, so she took her to a quiet corner, helped her adjust her costume and headpiece, did deep breathing with her, and played a selection from 'The Nutcracker' to help her relax. When the performance began, she stayed by her side throughout at the side curtain, whispering softly every time there was a wonderful act to distract her from nervousness. Although her daughter had missed the lead role because of health reasons, she smiled brightly and moved precisely in the group dance. After the performance, she hugged her tightly, and her daughter's words — 'Mom, it's enough to be happy dancing' — made her eyes well up instantly, turning all her guilt and worry into gratitude.
location: Pastor Mao Jimei Memorial Hall, 139 Ma Tau Chung Road, Kowloon City District, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region

name: Celebration lunch and buying a cake for best friend
description: After the show ended, her husband went home first to prepare for the afternoon's work, while she walked with the two children to the New Shanghai Kitchen Chinese restaurant. On the way, she bought a small bunch of daisies for her daughter at a flower shop. For lunch, they ordered her daughter's favorite char siu spaghetti and iced lemon tea, and her son's curry beef brisket rice. The children ate with a hearty appetite, sharing stories about the performance and funny school incidents. After the meal, they quickly walked to the adjacent Cakez Caf, where she selected and bought an exquisite mango mille-crepe cake gift box for her best friend Lin Jiaxin, asked the clerk to put it in a gift bag, and confirmed it could be brought directly to the cafe tomorrow afternoon.
location: New Shanghai Kitchen Chinese Restaurant, 7 Tak Fung Street, Hung Hom, Hong Kong

name: Family time at noon: walking, sorting photos, and chatting
description: After the meal, the family of three slowly walked home, enjoying the pleasant afternoon. Once home, I transferred the photos and videos of the performance from my phone to the tablet, picked out a few favorites with the children for the family album, and promised my daughter I would send the video of her best dance to Grandma. Then my mother handed me steaming hot pear water, my father shared the newspaper news about the route change for next weekend's Hong Kong Marathon, and my mother talked about her plan to go flower viewing with friends in Victoria Park tomorrow afternoon. Sipping the drink, I leaned back on the sofa for a short rest, savoring this rare moment of leisure.
location: Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, Kowloon City District, Hung Hom, Whampoa Garden residential estate

name: Focus on studying the CFP tax module
description: Changed into loose loungewear, went into the study, turned off phone notifications, and began studying the CFP tax module, focusing on the chapter "Tax Avoidance and Optimization of Capital Gains Tax and Dividend Tax in International Family Investment Portfolios." Carefully took two pages of notes and used a red pen to mark corrections on the 5 accompanying practice questions, deeply thinking about the financial planning logic in the case studies.
location: Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, Kowloon City District, Hung Hom, Whampoa Garden residential estate

After the workout, my heart rate rose noticeably. I wiped off sweat with a towel, took a few sips of electrolyte water, and felt full of energy.
location: Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, Kowloon City District, Hung Hom, Whampoa Garden residential estate

Today she planned to finish the leaf veins on the maple leaves, using skilled stitching to outline the clear texture of the veins. The cat Bailey jumped onto her lap as usual, purring. While listening to a drama, she threaded the needle and felt extremely relaxed and healed.
location: Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, Kowloon City District, Hung Hom, Whampoa Garden residential estate

name: Assist with checking homework and preparing dinner.

Then went to the kitchen, cut the washed choy sum according to her mother's taste and set it aside, and helped put the steamed dried fish into the pot to prepare dinner.
location: Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, Kowloon City District, Hung Hom, Whampoa Garden residential estate

name: Family dinner and warm conversation
description: The whole family sat around enjoying the hearty dinner her mother had cooked: steamed grass carp, stir-fried choy sum with garlic, a nice soup (pork bone soup with green radish and carrot), and steamed pork ribs in black bean sauce. At the table, the daughter excitedly shared stories from backstage at the performance again, while the son talked about his weekend football training plans. The atmosphere was lively and warm, full of laughter.
location: Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, Kowloon City District, Hung Hom, Whampoa Garden residential estate

name: Family movie night
description: After dinner, my husband and I cleaned up the dining table together: he washed the dishes while I wiped the table. He then washed the grapes and blueberries, and I took out chips, popcorn, and nuts from the snack cabinet and set them on the coffee table to prepare for family movie night. We all curled up on the sofa to watch the animated film Moana. I leaned against my husband's shoulder while the children watched with great interest while eating snacks. The part where Moana insists on being herself reminded me of my daughter's performance during the day, and my heart was filled with warmth. Midway through, my husband got up and cooked a bowl of noodles for our son as a late-night snack.
location: Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, Kowloon City District, Hung Hom, Whampoa Garden residential estate

name: Children's bedtime routine and personal meditation.
description: After the movie, she hurried the children to brush their teeth and wash their faces. First she read the picture book Lulu the Ballerina to her daughter, who soon fell asleep. Then she checked her son's football shoes, knee pads, and change of clothes for tomorrow's football class, and confirmed they were in the backpack. Back in the study alone, she opened a meditation app and did a 10-minute body scan meditation to release the day's fatigue and emotion. Then in her diary she wrote down three moving moments from today: her daughter's words "being happy is enough," her husband's silent companionship, and her mother's slow-cooked soup.
location: Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, Kowloon City District, Hung Hom, Whampoa Garden residential estate

Lying in bed, I talked softly with my husband, sharing my feelings about our daughter's growth, chatting about his work schedule next week, and discussing the logistics of picking up and dropping off our son for football class. Then I did my bedtime washing and carefully completed my basic skincare routine (cleanser, toner, serum, eye cream). Thinking about tomorrow afternoon's date with my best friend, I felt happy.

location: Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, Kowloon City District, Hung Hom, Whampoa Garden residential estate

Her husband Zhang Weiming also got up, and the couple divided the work: Yu Xiaowei took out the braised chicken wings from last night, sliced toast, and cheese slices from the refrigerator, quickly made ham-and-cheese sandwiches and egg-salad sandwiches, and washed the grapes and blueberries and put them in a food storage container. Zhang Weiming checked the family's two adult mountain bikes and his son's children's mountain bike, oiled the chains, tested the tire pressure, and double-checked that their daughter's safety seat was secure.

Then she woke up her son Zhang Zixuan and daughter Zhang Yuxin on time, and tied her daughter's hair into a ponytail. The whole family sat together for breakfast: milk, cereal, and freshly made sandwiches. She also filled her daughter's B.Duck water bottle with warm water. Zixuan was very excited and quickly put on his sportswear by himself.
location: Whampoa Garden residential estate, Kowloon City District, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region

location: Whampoa Garden residential estate, Kowloon City District, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region

name: Set off for Tai Wai Station and rent cycling equipment.
description: The family of four wore lightweight sportswear. Yu Xiaowei carried a backpack full of picnic food and water, while Zhang Weiming carried a backpack containing a first-aid kit, sunscreen, and children's helmets. Zixuan rode his own small mountain bike, and the couple each pushed an adult bike. They walked to Whampoa Station, took the Kwun Tong Line to Kowloon Tong Station, then transferred to the East Rail Line and arrived at Tai Wai Station, taking about 30 minutes in total. At the Lianxing bicycle rental shop at Exit A of Tai Wai Station, they installed a rear rack and a child seat (for the daughter) on Zhang Weiming's bike, and rented adult helmets. Yu Xiaowei carefully adjusted her son's helmet strap and checked the brakes. Once everything was ready, they officially set off from the entrance of the Tai Wai cycling path.

name: Family bike ride along Tolo Harbour
description: A family of four cycled along the scenic Tolo Harbour waterfront cycling path. Yu Xiaowei led at the front, controlling the pace, maintaining a safe speed, and looking back from time to time; Zhang Weiming rode behind the son with their daughter on his bike, encouraging him to keep up his cadence. Midway, they rested for 15 minutes at the lookout on the Pak Shek Kok Promenade, drinking water and taking photos. The children were very excited to see the sailboats across the harbor and the mountain views of Pat Sin Leng.
location: Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, Tolo Harbour waterfront cycling path

name: Autumn picnic by Plover Cove Lake
description: Arrived at the grassy area beside the main dam of Plover Cove Reservoir in Tai Mei Tuk, found a patch of shade, and spread out the picnic mat. The family enjoyed homemade sandwiches, chicken wings, and fruit. A gentle breeze blew across the lake, with ripples on the blue water. After the meal, Zixuan and Dad played frisbee on the grass, while the daughter pulled Yu Xiaowei to look at the little fish in the lake and the kite flyers in the distance. Yu Xiaowei felt utterly relaxed and happy.
location: The grassy area beside the main dam of Plover Cove Reservoir, Tai Po District, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region

name: Cycling back, returning the bike, and heading home.
description: After packing up all belongings and trash, they started the return trip. They slowed down and rested for 15 minutes near Science Park, where Yu Xiaowei shared cookies with the children to replenish their energy. Back in Tai Wai, they successfully returned the rented bicycles and equipment, and Zixuan proudly announced to the shop owner, "I rode the whole way." Then the family took the MTR back to Whampoa Garden, discussing the day's fun along the way.
location: Along the route from MTR Tai Wai Station in Sha Tin District to Whampoa Garden in Kowloon City District, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region

Yu Xiaowei and her husband took turns quickly showering and changing into dry loungewear. Weiming wiped the children's bicycles clean and put them away. Then the family held a brief family meeting in the living room. Yu Xiaowei praised the children's perseverance and performance. Everyone shared the happiest moments of the ride, and she formally proposed making 'Family Outdoor Day' a quarterly event, which passed unanimously. They had a lively discussion about the next activity (going to Tai Tong in Yuen Long to see red leaves in November, or hiking on Lamma Island in December), settled on two options, and decided to vote next time. Yu Xiaowei solemnly recorded the plan in her phone memo.
location: Whampoa Garden residential estate, Kowloon City District, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region

Then she took out the cake and the book, placed the little sunflower on a napkin, creating a warm atmosphere.

The two ordered two flat whites and, while sharing the cake, talked about Jiaxin's hard work preparing for the exam, the joy of passing, and the fun cycling stories from Yu Xiaowei's family. Laughter was endless and the atmosphere was warm.
